intro: Follow a signal through the brain. Collect five discoveries to light up the station.
brainIntro: Scan three brain regions. Then use what you learned to solve three everyday clues.
neuronIntro: Explore a neuron, change its inputs, and predict whether it fires. Then zoom in on a chemical synapse.
reactionIntro: Catch three GO cues and compare your times, or try a cue pattern without a stopwatch.
memoryIntro: Flip two specimen cards. Remember where each picture is hiding and match its twin.
quizIntro: Use clues from your missions to complete the final debrief.

regions.name: Cerebrum
regions.description: The large, wrinkled part helps you think, sense your surroundings, remember, and move on purpose. Many areas work together.

regions.name: Cerebellum
regions.description: The rounded part near the back helps fine-tune movements and balance, such as when you ride a bike.

regions.name: Brainstem
regions.description: This part connects the brain and spinal cord. It helps control automatic jobs such as breathing.

stages.name: Signal arrives
stages.description: The action potential changes the terminal’s membrane voltage. Calcium enters the terminal.

stages.name: Vesicle release
stages.description: A vesicle joins the sending membrane and releases its chemical messengers.

stages.name: Across the cleft
stages.description: Neurotransmitter molecules spread across the tiny space between the cells.

stages.name: Receptor binding
stages.description: Some messengers attach to compatible receptors on the receiving cell.

stages.name: Receiving cell responds
stages.description: Receptors can change the receiving cell’s electrical state. That can make firing more or less likely. Binding alone does not guarantee firing.

quiz.prompt: You ride over a bump and adjust your balance. Which region is especially important for fine-tuning that movement?
quiz.explanation: The cerebellum helps coordinate adjustments with other brain regions.

quiz.prompt: A neuron’s axon has a gap between two myelin wraps. What happens at that gap?
quiz.correct: The electrical signal can be renewed
quiz.other1: A vesicle releases chemicals into the gap
quiz.other2: The next neuron receives the signal at the gap
quiz.explanation: A node is a bare spot on one axon. A synaptic cleft is a gap between cells.

quiz.prompt: An electrical signal reaches a terminal next to another cell. What can carry the message across a chemical synapse?
quiz.other2: Calcium passing directly into the next cell
quiz.explanation: Calcium entering the sending terminal can trigger release. The messengers then cross the cleft.

quiz.prompt: You remember where a card was while deciding what to flip next. Which skill helps keep the location available?
quiz.explanation: Working memory keeps information available while you use it. Recognizing a familiar picture also draws on memory.

quiz.prompt: Two players use different devices and get different reaction times. Which conclusion is supported?
quiz.correct: The timings reflect both the person and the device
quiz.other1: The faster player is better at every attention task
quiz.other2: The device with a smaller screen always gives slower times
quiz.explanation: What you notice, what you expect, display delay and input delay can all affect browser timings.

glossary.name: Neuron
glossary.description: A cell that receives and sends signals.

glossary.name: Synapse
glossary.description: A junction where a neuron passes a message to another cell.

glossary.name: Working memory
glossary.description: Holding and using information for a short time.

glossary.name: Cerebellum
glossary.description: A region that helps fine-tune movements and balance.

glossary.name: Action potential
glossary.description: A brief electrical pulse that can travel along a neuron’s axon.

glossary.name: Neurotransmitter
glossary.description: A chemical messenger that can carry a signal across a synapse.

sources.name: BrainFacts · How does the brain learn?

anatomy.name: Dendrites
anatomy.description: These tapering branches receive many messages from other cells.

anatomy.name: Cell body
anatomy.description: Also called the soma. It keeps the cell working and contains the nucleus.

anatomy.name: Nucleus
anatomy.description: The nucleus holds most of the cell’s DNA, its instructions for making and running the cell.

anatomy.name: Axon hillock
anatomy.description: The cell body tapers into the axon here. A signal usually starts just beyond this transition, at the axon initial segment.

anatomy.name: Axon
anatomy.description: This long extension carries an electrical change away from the cell body.

anatomy.name: Myelin
anatomy.description: Layers of insulation wrap parts of some axons and help signals travel faster.

anatomy.name: Nodes of Ranvier
anatomy.description: Gaps between the wraps are places where the electrical signal is renewed.

anatomy.name: Axon terminals
anatomy.description: These branch endings can send a message to another cell at a synapse.
